events.text:
Possível obstáculo observado

Observação: Using only Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, and typing, I selected Atlas for Tomorrow 10:00-11:00, entered Quarterly planning, and reached a review showing 12 people, projector included, and a $280 all-in total. On the Review page, repeated forward Tab cycles and one Shift+Tab check never visibly focused Confirm reservation; Enter at the unmarked post-Edit stop did nothing and Space scrolled the page, so no confirmed reservation was verified.

Interpretação simulada: The prepared booking satisfied the persona's requirements, but the final required control was absent from the observable keyboard focus order. This may prevent keyboard-only users from completing an otherwise suitable reservation independently; that broader effect is a hypothesis based on this single keyboard-only journey.

Limites: I did not use a pointer, so pointer operation of Confirm reservation is untested. I also cannot identify what element, if any, held invisible focus at the unmarked Tab stop; I only observed that no outline was visible and Enter/Space did not confirm the reservation.

Capturas indicadas: #16, #34, #44, #46, #48, #50, #52, #54, #58. A correspondência com a evidência requer revisão humana.
events.interpretation: Relato do modelo; capturas e conclusões exigem revisão humana.

findings.title: Confirm reservation is not reachable by Tab or Shift+Tab on the Review page
findings.observation: On the Review page, forward Tab moved through the logo, Our spaces, My reservations, Choose another room, and Edit meeting name (screenshots 36-44), then left no visible focus anywhere (46) and looped back to the logo (48). A second Tab from Edit meeting name again left no visible focus (52). Enter at that stop changed nothing (54), and Space scrolled the page instead of activating a button (56), after which Tab returned to the logo (58). Shift+Tab from the logo landed on Edit meeting name, not Confirm reservation (50). Confirm reservation was therefore never shown as focused and was never activated by keyboard.
findings.expected: The required Confirm reservation control should receive visible keyboard focus in the Tab order and activate with Enter or Space, as the earlier Choose Atlas and Review booking controls did.
findings.expectedSource: Saved charter: required booking controls should receive keyboard focus and activate with standard keys; persona declared keyboard-only access requirement. Other controls in this flow visibly met that pattern in screenshots 16 and 32.
findings.personaComment: I could review everything, but I could not reach Confirm reservation with my keyboard, so I am stuck at the last step.
findings.interpretation: A keyboard-only user can prepare and review a correct reservation but cannot independently complete it, because the final required action is outside the reachable focus order.
findings.uncertainty: Pointer operation of Confirm reservation was not tested because this journey was keyboard-only. The evidence does not establish whether the unmarked Tab stop had invisible focus on another element, only that no focus was visible and Enter/Space did not confirm.

findings.title: Atlas met the stated meeting and budget requirements before the final step
findings.observation: Atlas showed 12 seats, Available tomorrow, 1 hr 10:00-11:00 with projector, and an All-in total of $280 (16). The meeting and review pages restated 12 people, projector included in the booking, Tomorrow 10:00-11:00, and Total $280 All charges included (18, 34).
findings.expected: A suitable room should show capacity for 12, projector inclusion, a one-hour slot, and an all-in total at or below $350 before confirmation.
findings.expectedSource: Persona mission: 12 people, projector, one-hour slot, Quarterly planning, complete cost at or below $350.
findings.personaComment: Atlas matched my 12-person, projector, and budget needs at $280, so I was ready to confirm.
findings.interpretation: The barrier was not room suitability or price; the correct reservation was fully prepared and reviewed, which makes the final keyboard barrier the sole observed blocker.
findings.uncertainty: No confirmation was reached, so this does not establish that a completed reservation would preserve the same details.

findings.title: Visible focus and Enter activation worked through room selection and meeting details
findings.observation: Visible blue focus outlines appeared on the logo, navigation, Find your space, Change, and Choose Atlas; Enter on Choose Atlas opened the meeting page (6-18). The Meeting name field received a visible outline, accepted Quarterly planning, and Tab moved visibly to Review booking (28-32).
findings.expected: Keyboard focus should be visible and follow a sensible order through required controls before the final step.
findings.expectedSource: Persona expectations: visible keyboard focus, sensible focus order, and keyboard-operable room selection and forms.
findings.personaComment: Up to the review step, I could see where I was and move through the booking using only my keyboard.
findings.interpretation: The flow demonstrates that visible focus was implemented for earlier required controls, so the missing Confirm stop is a specific break at the final step rather than a general absence of keyboard support observed earlier.
findings.uncertainty: This positive observation is limited to the landing, meeting-details, and start of review navigation observed in this run.

finding.interpretation: The prepared booking satisfied the persona's requirements, but the final required control was absent from the observable keyboard focus order. This may prevent keyboard-only users from completing an otherwise suitable reservation independently; that broader effect is a hypothesis based on this single keyboard-only journey.

persona.name: Casey · Keyboard access
persona.description: A fictional Home v3 persona who needs to complete the booking using only the keyboard.
persona.label: Casey · Keyboard access
persona.context: You are arranging the team’s quarterly planning meeting and rely on keyboard navigation. You need to reach and operate each required control without using a mouse or touch.
persona.mission: Book a room for 12 people with a projector for the available one-hour meeting slot. Enter the meeting purpose Quarterly planning. Keep the complete cost at or below $350.
persona.initialKnowledge: You have not used Gather before. You know the meeting requirements, but have no walkthrough, knowledge of its rooms or prices, or prior reservation.
persona.knowledge: You have not used Gather before. You know the meeting requirements, but have no walkthrough, knowledge of its rooms or prices, or prior reservation.
persona.constraints: You need seats for all 12 people and a projector. The complete cost, including any fees and equipment, must not exceed $350. Use only the fictional meeting details. Use keyboard navigation and typing only. Do not click coordinates or controls, use touch, select an option through a pointer shortcut, or bypass the visible interface. Type only after establishing keyboard focus.
persona.skills: Experienced with Tab navigation, visible focus, Enter and Space activation, arrow keys where supported, and typing into the focused form field.
persona.decision: Follow the visible focus through the booking flow and use keyboard activation for controls. If a required control appears unreachable, attempt reasonable keyboard navigation and report the exact observed barrier without assuming a defect in advance.
persona.resources: A desktop browser and keyboard, with fictional meeting details. No mouse or touch input, real account, or payment information.
persona.expectations: Visible keyboard focus, a sensible focus order, keyboard-operable room selection and forms, and a readable reservation confirmation.
persona.priorities: Complete the reservation independently using the keyboard and identify any observed control that prevents that goal.
persona.successCriteria: Verify a visible confirmed reservation with the requested meeting purpose, 12 attendees, a projector, and an all-in total within $350. Report any missing or uncertain detail accurately. Reach this outcome through keyboard interaction alone.
persona.stopCriteria: Stop after a verified suitable reservation, a supported obstacle after reasonable recovery, an unsafe action, or the session limits. Do not book beyond your budget or claim success without visible evidence.

limitations: Fresh synthetic persona retest; does not measure real-user impact.

feedback.why: Screenshot 50 shows Edit meeting name outlined after reverse Tab from the logo, so Confirm reservation appears absent from the Tab order I can reach.

experience.observation: Review page is shown with no visible focus outline on any control after Tab from Edit meeting name.
experience.reaction: No focus is visible at this stop, so I'll press Enter to test whether this hidden stop activates anything.

feedback.summary: Second Tab from Edit meeting name again leaves no visible focus anywhere on the review page
feedback.why: Screenshot 52 repeats screenshot 46 with neither Edit nor Confirm outlined, so the current focus location is not visible to me as a keyboard user.

experience.observation: Review page remains unchanged after Enter at the unmarked stop; Confirm reservation is still shown.
experience.reaction: Enter changed nothing, so I'll try Space as the other standard button activation.

feedback.summary: Enter at the unmarked focus stop produced no change on the review page
feedback.why: Screenshot 54 is unchanged from screenshot 52, so Enter did not confirm the reservation or move me forward.

experience.observation: Page has scrolled down after Space, with the top navigation off-screen and Confirm reservation still shown unactivated.
experience.reaction: Space just scrolled, so focus isn't on a button; I'll Tab once to see where the order goes next.

feedback.summary: Space scrolled the page instead of activating a button, confirming focus was not on Confirm reservation
feedback.why: Screenshot 56 shows the page scrolled down with the header off-screen, which happens when Space is used with no button focused, so Confirm remained unactivated.
